I'm scanning through the residue coordinates looking for atoms that sit unusually close together, checking side chains like MSE 13 and nearby leucines for potential steric overlap.

Given the scale of the structure, I'm switching to mapping out approximate CA positions along the helical chain to spot which residues come into close spatial contact with each other.

Continuing to list out the coordinate values...

Still generating coordinate data...

Looking at the full trace of CA positions through residue 89, this looks like a helical bundle structure, and I'm noting potential long-range contacts between early and later residues.

I'm checking a few more residue pairs for proximity, but most distances I'm finding are too large to indicate a real clash. I'm now scanning across the different helical segments to see if any of them come close enough together to matter structurally.

I should try a different strategy since manual pairwise distance checking is inefficient here. Since these puzzles often deliberately introduce a single severe clash, I want to focus on residues whose CAs are close in space but far apart in sequence, then check their side chain atoms specifically for that violation.

I'm computing more pairwise CA distances between helix1 and helix2 residues, mostly finding distances too large for contact except a couple near sequence-adjacent pairs like residue 26 vs 24. Continuing to scan for closer contacts elsewhere in the chain.

Given this looks like a compact helical bundle rather than a coiled coil, I'm checking whether the clash might come from side chains at positions i, i+3/i+4 within a single helix rather than between helices, testing specific atom pairs like MSE13's SE against nearby LEU and VAL side chain carbons to see if any fall within clash distance.

I'm scanning other neighboring regions—residues 34, 40-58, and 41-51 involving TYR, HIS, GLU, and LYS side chains—computing distances between ring and chain atoms, but nothing so far falls close enough to explain the clash. I'm now checking the LYS52 NZ against SER49 OG to see if that pair is the culprit.

I'm continuing to scan nearby residue pairs for close contacts, checking distances between side chain atoms of MSE66, ALA65, LEU62, ALA61, LEU57, ALA54, and HIS53, but none of these are turning up significant clashes so far.

I'm now checking PHE56's ring against ASN60, GLN12's side chain against ASN15 and GLU8/11, and LYS17 against ASP18, finding one borderline distance around 3.7 between LYS17 NZ and ASP18 OD1, with the rest too far apart to matter.

I move on to scanning PHE20's aromatic ring against nearby residues like ALA65 and VAL26, spotting another close contact of roughly 3.9 to ALA65's CB, but nothing else striking so far in this region.

I shift to LEU21's side chain, checking distances to ASP27, GLU28, and ALA30, but none come out particularly close. I then pivot to the buried helix pair around residues 30-34 versus 54-58, and find PHE31's ring making a tight ~3.7 contact with ALA61's CB, though other nearby leucines like LEU58 and LEU57 don't show anything notable.

Then I move to TYR34's ring, finding it sits about 4.0 from ALA54's CB, while VAL55 and GLU40 don't come close. I check PHE31 against TYR34 and move on to GLU35's side chain, which doesn't show any nearby leucine contacts.

I look at the 37-39 versus 50-51 region, testing LEU37's CD1/CD2 against GLU50 without finding anything tight, then check VAL39's CG2 against GLU50's CB, landing around 3.9. I glance at PRO41's CG for the 41-44 versus 51 region, then start comparing the 44-49 helix against the 40s residues.

Now I'm shifting focus entirely to the 70-89 region, checking ARG76's guanidinium group against SER72 and PHE71 without finding proximity, then testing it against LYS79 and ARG80 with no close hits either. I find ILE77's CD1 sits about 4.6 from ARG80's CZ and closer, around 3.9, to ARG80's NH2, so I start pulling up ILE77's CG1 coordinates to check further.

Nothing severe turns up there. I check MSE81's selenium and carbon atoms against nearby residues like LEU84 and ALA85, finding no clashes, though the SE-CE and SE-CG bond distances look normal while the CE-CG distance (2.41, going through the selenium at an unusually tight ~76° angle instead of the expected ~98°) suggests an internal geometry quirk rather than a real interatomic clash between residues. Since there's only one chain, I rule out interchain contacts and decide to switch strategies, thinking I should map out the structure on a spatial grid to systematically check proximity instead of testing residue pairs one at a time.

I try scanning specific tight-turn regions like residues 88-89 and check SER89 and ASP86 side chains, but nothing clashes there either. I consider searching for atoms with near-duplicate coordinates and start estimating side-chain centroid positions residue by residue as a more efficient way to flag close pairs before verifying them atom-by-atom, beginning with MSE1's selenium position.

Still mapping out residue coordinates...

I'm now scanning through pairs of nearby side-chain tips to check for close contacts, computing distances between atoms like NZ, CZ, and ring atoms across different residues to spot potential clashes or interactions.

Checking LYS79 NZ against GLU83's carboxylate oxygens, I get a distance of about 2.1 Å, which is suspiciously short even for a salt bridge — that's likely a clash rather than a legitimate interaction.

This confirms the OE1-NZ distance at 2.06 Å is genuinely severe, close to the CD-NZ distance at 3.0 Å which fits the geometry. I want to check if anything is even shorter, so I'm scanning other nearby residue pairs like LYS79 CE against GLU83 OE1, which comes out around 3.0, and starting to check ARG76's guanidinium group too.

Continuing to scan atom pairs systematically for close contacts...

ASP18 OD1 and LYS17 NZ come out around 3.67 Å apart, and GLU35 OE2 to LYS17 NZ lands near 3.5 Å, so both look like plausible salt bridges. Most of the other GLU/ASP-LYS pairings I check remain too far apart to count.

LYS79 NZ to GLU83 OE1 at 2.06 Å stands out as a strong salt bridge candidate. I'm now scanning hydrophobic side chain contacts for tight packing, checking distances between residues like PHE20/ALA65, ILE16/MSE13, LEU58/VAL55, and others, but most pairs are coming in above 4 Å and only a few atoms land in the 3.5 Å range worth noting.

Continuing to check distances between His10, His51, and nearby residue side chains for possible ring contacts.

That distance comes to 3.6, so no clash there. I've already checked HIS51 against 54/55, and HIS43 versus VAL39 is too far apart in the z-direction to matter. Now I'm checking HIS53's ND1 against nearby PHE56 residues for potential contacts.

Working through more distance checks: PHE56's ring against HIS53's CD2 comes back negative, SER49's OG against LYS52 and HIS53 also shows no proximity issue, and SER47's OG versus GLU50's CG lands right at the edge around 3.1, which is fine. Now moving on to check VAL44's CG1 position against nearby residues.

Checking GLN12 CG against ASN15 CB, still no proximity there, then testing ASN15 CG versus GLU11 CD for a possible contact.

The worst clash so far remains LYS79 NZ to GLU83 OE1 at 2.06 Å. I'm now scanning backbone-to-side-chain distances near the turns at residues 74-76 and 88-89, checking LYS79's NZ and CB against nearby arginine and glutamate atoms in that region, but nothing closer is turning up yet.

I'll keep checking other residue pairs across the helix segments for possible close contacts, particularly between sequence-distant carbon atoms that might overlap.

Checking more residue pairs between the two helices—17 vs 61 and 20 vs 65—both giving distances around 9-10, confirming the helix-helix spacing is consistently in that range.

Now I'm mapping which side chains point inward between helix 1-20 and helix 26-40, checking PHE20/ALA65, ILE16/LEU62, MSE13/GLY59, LEU9/VAL55 pairs at close contact distances of 3.9-4.5, then moving to LYS17/PHE31 where the LYS17 CD atom sits about 3.4 from PHE31's ring carbon.

Continuing between helix 26-40 and helix 50-70, I'm confirming PHE31's ring maintains close contact around 3.7 with ALA61's side chain, and now checking whether TYR34 makes any close contacts with ALA54's beta carbon or nearby residues.

I find LEU37 sits near HIS53 at roughly 4.1-4.2 apart, so I'll note that contact and move on to check interactions between the 41-49 helix segment and the rest.

Now I'm scanning the 70-89 helix against 50-70 for close contacts — PHE71 near ALA67/74 and GLY75 come back too far, and I'm checking ILE77's side chain against SER73 and ARG80 to see if any distances fall within range.

LYS79-GLU83 comes out as the closest pair so far at 2.06. Before settling on that, I want to double-check backbone contacts near residues 85-88, the 41-42 turn region, and the MSE1 N-terminus, then systematically scan all charged/polar tip pairs for sub-2.5 distances — starting with LYS46 NZ against ASP38's oxygens and LYS3 NZ against ASP4, neither of which look close enough.

I'm scanning for other repulsive clashes among glutamate and aspartate residues, and checking serine/threonine hydroxyl contacts too, but nothing else stands out — the 2.06 Å LYS79-GLU83 distance still looks like the most severe steric clash.

Checking a few more nonadjacent residue pairs like 84-86 and 22 for close backbone contacts, but nothing under 2.0 Å is turning up yet.

Testing GLU83 CG against LYS79 NZ gives a distance of about 4.3 Å, ruling that pair out too. So the closest nonadjacent pair I've found remains A:K79--A:E83.
